evals.prompt: I've got 15 minutes at our team meeting on Friday to talk about the new expenses process. Here are my notes: submit within 30 days, photo of the receipt in the app, manager approves, finance pays on the 25th, common mistakes are missing receipts and wrong cost codes. Can you make me something visual to click through while I talk? I'll be sharing my screen in Teams.
evals.expected_output: Asks up to 3 numbered questions with a recommended answer each, including a short slide plan table with click counts, then builds a single light-theme HTML file from the template with about 5-7 slides, one idea and one moving visual per slide, everyday examples, grouped clicks, no external scripts, and checks it in a browser.
expectations: Asks no more than 3 numbered questions, each with options and a 'Recommend' line, before building
Proposes a slide plan with the number of clicks per slide
Produces one HTML file with no external script, font or image URLs
Uses a light background and no constant background animation
Keeps on-screen text short (headline plus a few words per slide)
Uses data-auto to group related steps so the whole talk needs far fewer clicks than build steps
Clicks through the finished file in a browser, or says it could not

evals.prompt: Use my company theme. I'm doing a 20-minute session for the marketing team on how our paid search changed this year: we moved budget from broad match to exact match, cost per click went down 18%, conversions up 12%, and we cut 40 wasted keywords. I'll demo the new reporting dashboard live halfway through. Make me a visual aid to click through on Teams.
evals.expected_output: Reads the context file for brand and audience, asks at most 3 questions with recommendations, then builds a themed single-file aid designed for paid search: metrics that count up, a before/after of the budget split, a demo-intro slide and a close. It does not carry over prompting, skill or Copilot content from the template's history.
expectations: Looks for visual-aid-context.md in the workspace and context.md next to SKILL.md before asking about the theme
Applies the theme by changing only the :root variables and the wordmark/footer text
Uses a metrics-style visual for the CPC and conversion figures, with the figures given by the user and none invented
Contains no leftover template placeholder text and no content about prompting, skills or Copilot
Includes a slide that introduces the live demo
Does not add the presenter's job title unless asked

evals.prompt: Just did a practice run of the visual aid. Slide 4's before text changes before I finish reading it, the ticks from slide 5 hang around when slide 6 comes in, and the little numbers in the labels don't match the counter at the bottom.
evals.expected_output: Fixes all three in the existing file: keeps the before text visible and brings the after in beside it on its own click, replaces any transition:all with explicit properties so nothing lingers, removes the section numbers from labels, then re-checks those slides in a browser.
expectations: Shows before and after side by side instead of swapping text in place, with a separate click for the after
Finds and replaces transition: all on elements inside slides with an explicit property list
Removes the numbers from the eyebrow labels rather than renumbering the counter
Re-checks the changed slides in a browser after fixing

evals.prompt: I'm meeting our head of operations tomorrow to talk through a proposed booking system: requests come in from the website, email and phone, get checked and de-duplicated, land in one shared calendar, and staff, managers and a reporting dashboard read from it. There are three ways we could roll it out and a few open questions. I don't want slides, just one page I can scroll on Teams while we talk. Keep it visual, no walls of text.
evals.expected_output: Picks the one-page format, asks at most 3 questions with recommendations, then builds a single light-theme scrolling page from the one-page template: a system diagram with the inputs, check step, shared calendar and users renamed for the topic, phases, the rollout options with one suggested, questions and risks as short chips, a small mind map, and a working light/dark toggle, with no paragraphs and no external dependencies.
expectations: Uses assets/one-page-template.html rather than the slide template
Renames every diagram box for the booking system and leaves no template placeholder text
Has no paragraphs: labels and one-line details only
Keeps the light/dark toggle and defaults to light
Produces one HTML file with no external script, font or image URLs
Checks the page at 1366 and about 400 wide in both themes, or says it could not
